A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A-C are readable and can be matched despite pagination and presentation changes.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic-network, image-classification and transfer-learning experiments. Appendix C reports additional trained-weight singular-value results.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification, transfer-learning and Appendix C results and reports revised synthetic-network results in Figures 4 and 9-11.

M1.justification: The DLN model, MSE objective, gradient-descent procedure, orthogonal initialization and feature-compression/discrimination metrics are retained. Changes concern experimental configurations and documentation rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 revises the simulated input distribution: normalized perturbations are generated from uniform [0,1] samples instead of standard-normal samples. FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and the classification and transfer-learning tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The same MLP, hybrid and linear-network comparators remain in the corresponding experiments, including the MLP-versus-hybrid comparison in Figure 3. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5.1.2 changes the stated accuracy summary from best to average, and Section 5.2.1 changes balancedness normalization from L to L-1. Figure 11 replaces depths 8/16 with 5/8. Figure 4 changes its depth labels from 9/9 to 6/10, although Section 5.2.2 still specifies nine-layer networks, leaving that configuration inconsistent.

E4.justification: Figures 10-11 revise existing nonlinear-network and initialization-sensitivity analyses, particularly whether discrimination increases under default initialization. Figure 11 removes the 16-layer case and adds a five-layer case. The projection-head analysis and Appendix C low-rankness analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains its shaded bands and five-run reporting, but v2 drops the caption's identification of the bands as standard deviations. The ten-run reporting for Figure 6 and three-seed standard deviations for Figure 13 remain unchanged; no increase in runs is documented.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 9-11 substantially replace the synthetic evidence supporting feature evolution. For example, Figure 9 at initialization scale 0.3 reports first-layer discrimination around 0.80 instead of 0.98 under revised data generation. Figure 11 now shows increasing discrimination under default initialization, replacing v1's inconsistent trend, although its caption retains the old finding. Changed conditions prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The principal assumptions, Theorems 1-3, Proposition 1 and their proofs are retained; class balance remains in Section 2.1 despite its removal from Assumption 1. The mathematical definition of averaged balancedness is corrected from division by L to L-1. New Appendix B.4 merely makes the existing implication from Theorems 2 and 3 explicit.

C1.justification: The contribution summary corrects the discrimination slope from O(θ+4δ) to O((θ+4δ)/L) and explicitly asserts that the framework can extend to nonlinear networks. The abstract and conclusion retain the central DLN feature-evolution and transfer-learning claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges that Assumption 1 simplifies analysis and may fail empirically, and clarifies that the transfer-learning argument relies on an empirical compression-transferability correlation. Conversely, Section 3.2 drops approximation qualifiers around GD solutions, and Section 5.3.1 removes the earlier limitation concerning discrimination under default initialization.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies cross-entropy training for the linear probes in Section 5.1.1 and explicitly states that the implementation uses Python. It revises the hardware description to an A40-equipped server and explicitly includes FashionMNIST. The repository link was already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds LL19, PSG18 and XBSD+18 concerning homogeneous networks and initialization, while removing EP21, JZW+23 and RBF22. It sharpens the distinction from the empirical work HS23, but retains the broader positioning relative to neural collapse, DLNs and NTK.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Background and Motivation subsection, topic headings, bulleted explanations and an appendix proof roadmap. Several assumption, transfer-learning and experimental passages are rewritten, while the main section order and most substantive exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: All 14 figures are retained. Several plots receive revised axes, markers, legends and captions; Figure 12 changes marker styles without changing its results. Figures 7-8 move into the experimental discussion, and a typeface change reflows the document while preserving its basic layout.

improvement.justification: Useful probing details, clearer qualifications and the corrected balancedness normalization are outweighed by new inconsistencies in experimental reporting. Figure 4's six- and ten-layer labels conflict with Section 5.2.2, while Figure 11's increasing discrimination conflicts with its retained caption. Figure 3 also loses the explanation of its uncertainty bands. These changes weaken interpretation and reproducibility of the empirical evidence, although the core theory and proofs remain intact.
